# cc-account-switcher — Agent Context

`ccswitch` is a multi-account AI coding-agent session manager: a CLI core plus a web-hosted,
mobile-accessible interface for running and switching between live agent sessions across
several accounts, with automatic usage-aware account rotation.

**Governance:** all work MUST comply with the project constitution at
`.specify/memory/constitution.md` (v1.2.0, Principles I–VII). Notably: never fork/patch a native
agent binary, and gate experimental vendor surfaces (I); account = one engine-scoped identity,
strict per-process isolation, at most one credential authority (II); verify against the real
binary/API, not assumptions (III); security-first, exposure-conditional auth (IV); TDD + quality
gates (V); single source of truth / no dead code (VI); modern vetted deps (VII).

Stack: Python FastAPI/Uvicorn + SQLAlchemy (SQLite in dev/tests, Postgres in prod) · React+Vite+TS
+ Tailwind/shadcn frontend · each session is a `claude` CLI driven through `claude-agent-sdk`
(`server/sessions/driver.py`), its events bridged to the browser over WebSocket · Tailscale-identity
auth. Specs live under `specs/` (`001-ccswitch-web` is the base feature, `002-*` session continuity /
X display, `003-gh-projects-integration`); design notes and plans under `docs/`.

## Architecture map

- `src/ccswitch/` — CLI core: accounts, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` isolation, creds, ledger, worktrees.
  Entry points `ccswitch`, `ccrun`, `ccmax` (`pyproject.toml`). Tests in `tests/`.
- `server/app.py` — the **edge**: FastAPI `create_app()`; `app = create_app()` runs at import, so
  importing the module already reads `CCSWITCH_*` env (see the test note below).
- `server/ipc/` — the **session daemon** (`python -m server.ipc`, `ccswitch-daemon.service`). It owns
  every live `claude` process; the edge talks to it over mTLS RPC. Remote hosts (e.g. rocky) run the
  same daemon in worker role (`CCSWITCH_DAEMON_ROLE`).
- `server/sessions/` — `SessionOrchestrator` (`orchestrator.py`) + per-session `driver.py` (SDK
  client, permissions, model switching). In remote mode the lifespan swaps `app.state.sessions` for
  `FleetOrchestrator` (`fleet_orchestrator.py`, routes via `fleet_router.py`) **after** routers are
  built — capture it lazily, never at router construction.
- `server/db/` — models, `init_db` reconcile, `clock.py` (see DB clock rule), `migrations/`.
- `server/deploy/` — deploy controller (`ccswitch-deploy-controller.service`); `server/sdlc/` —
  governance decisions enforced by `.claude/` (hook + managed deny rules + `REVIEW.md`).
- Other server packages: `api/` routers, `auth/`, `automations/`, `github/`, `pipeline/`, `pm/`,
  `library/`, `obs/`, `usage/`, `stt/`, `bridge/`.
- `web/src/` — `api/` (fetch + React Query hooks per domain), `session/` (event reducer +
  selectors), `shell/` (`AppShell`, nav, prompt dock), `components/`, `features/`, `ws/`.
- `deploy/` — systemd units + `deploy/README.md` (the ops runbook); `docs/runbooks/` for host
  procedures (Postgres cutover, onboarding a session runner, rocky).

## Completion workflow

When a unit of work is complete and verified (tests + lint green), finish it without being asked:
1. Branch off `origin/master` — `git fetch` first, then `git checkout -b <branch> origin/master`. NEVER
   branch off the local `master` ref: in a worktree it is a stale leftover (the deploy worktree owns
   `master`) and lags `origin/master` by hundreds of commits, so branching off it silently bases your
   work on ancient code. Never commit feature work directly to `master`.
2. Commit (end the message with the running model's `Co-Authored-By: Claude <model> <noreply@anthropic.com>`
   trailer). Write commit messages and PR bodies to a file and pass `-F` / `--body-file`: the Bash
   hook below denies any command whose *text* pairs a deploy verb with a prod word.
3. Push and open a PR via `gh pr create` (end body with the Claude Code trailer).
4. ALWAYS mark the PR ready for review (never leave it a draft) and ALWAYS flip auto-merge on
   once work is complete: open non-draft (omit `--draft`; if one slipped through, run
   `gh pr ready <#>`), then `gh pr merge <#> --squash --auto`. Both are required on every completed
   PR — a ready PR with auto-merge armed is the finished state.
Only hold off if the user said it's a prototype/WIP, or if verification is failing.

`master` is protected: PRs need the `lint-and-test`, `frontend` and `amendment` CI checks green and
the branch up to date with `master` before merging. `allow_update_branch` auto-rebases an out-of-date PR and
re-runs CI, so a green `--auto` PR lands without manual "Update branch" clicks. Branches are deleted
server-side on merge — don't pass `--delete-branch` (the `master` deploy worktree makes the local
delete fail). Merge queue is unavailable (user-owned repo); auto-merge + strict required checks
only *approximates* one, and only while master is quiet. A queue tests the prospective merge
result and holds a serialized position, so a PR at the front lands from that tested state.
`--auto` + strict instead re-tests the PR against a master that's free to move during the run, with
no position held — under a busy cadence (master advancing faster than a CI cycle takes) a PR can
be marked `BEHIND`, get rebased by `allow_update_branch`, and lose the race again, needing several
rebase-and-recheck cycles before it lands; each cycle is also a fresh exposure to any flaky check.
Admins may push directly in emergencies.

### Docs-only PRs: admin-merge, don't wait

A PR whose diff touches ONLY documentation may be squash-merged immediately with
`gh pr merge <N> --squash --admin` instead of waiting on `--auto`. The required checks exist to
catch broken code; none of them can be affected by a change that ships no code. Waiting makes a
docs PR pay a full ~12-minute `lint-and-test` cycle — and, under the rebase livelock above, often
several of them plus a fresh exposure to any flaky check — to prove nothing.

**Docs-only means every changed path matches `^docs/` or `\.md$` AND none of these:**

- `.specify/memory/constitution.md` — the governance document itself
- `.agents/instructions/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` — agent instructions. Markdown that changes
  how every agent behaves is *behaviour*, not documentation
- any path in `GUARDRAIL_PATHS` (`server/sdlc/governance.py`)
- `.github/**` — templates sit beside workflows and CODEOWNERS

The exclusions are the whole point. "It's only a `.md`" is exactly how a governance or behaviour
change slips in unreviewed, and for those paths `amendment` is the check that matters — the one
this shortcut would bypass. #1138 was a two-file `.md`-only PR that rewrote agent instructions;
a naive extension check would have merged it unread.

**Read the diff first** (`gh pr diff <N>`). The justification is "I read it and it ships no code",
never "the extension is `.md`". Never admin-merge a PR you have not read, and never use `--admin`
to bypass a check that is genuinely FAILING rather than merely pending — see
`triaging-stuck-prs`.

## Dev / testing

- Tests: server → `pytest server/tests/`; web → the npm scripts CI runs, in `web/`:
  `npm run typecheck` (`tsc -b`), `npm run lint` (eslint with `--max-warnings 0` — a bare `eslint`
  can pass where CI fails), `npm run test` (vitest), `npm run build`. E2E: `npm run test:e2e`
  (Playwright). Prompt evals: `python scripts/run_evals.py` (own workflow, `evals.yml`).
- The `lint-and-test` gate is **four** steps, not one: `ruff check src/ server/`, `mypy server/
  --ignore-missing-imports`, `pytest tests/` (core), `pytest server/tests/`. A green `server/tests/`
  run is not a green gate — mypy in particular catches what no test does (e.g. a `min()` over an
  httpx `Timeout` leg, which is typed `float | None`). Run all four before pushing.
- CI runs the server suite as `pytest server/tests/ -n auto --dist loadfile --timeout=300`. Serial
  it takes ~25 min; run it in the background with output tee'd to `/tmp/`, and never two full runs
  at once — the load spike gets the Bash call SIGKILLed (exit 137).
- **Unset `CCSWITCH_SESSIOND_*` and `CCSWITCH_DAEMON_ROLE` before running `server/tests/` locally.**
  `server/app.py` builds the app at import; a live shell's sessiond client-cert vars make it demand
  certs, and a worker `CCSWITCH_DAEMON_ROLE` turns ~90 tests into "No session with id" failures.
- Run the **full** `npm run test`, not just changed files: ~47 web test files manually mock
  `@/api/hooks`, so adding a hook to a shared component (e.g. `SessionList`) breaks tests in files you
  never touched. CI catches it; a changed-files run does not.
- **Bash hook trap:** `.claude/settings.json` runs `python3 .claude/hooks/prod-deploy-gate.py` as a
  `PreToolUse` hook on every Bash call. (1) It matches the command *text* (deploy|release|rollout|promote
  + prod|production), so a commit message or `grep` pattern containing both words is denied — put the
  text in a file. (2) The path is cwd-relative: a persisted `cd web` makes every subsequent Bash call
  fail until you `cd` back; use `(cd web && …)` subshells.
- **DB clock rule:** never use `func.now()` / `func.current_timestamp()`; use
  `server/db/clock.py:db_utc_now()`. Every column is naive UTC, but Postgres `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` is
  tz-aware and SQLite-only tests hide it — the last slip marked every prod session "Status unknown"
  (2026-09-03, #964).
- A fresh git worktree has no built env (network blocks `uv sync` of the ~70MB claude-agent-sdk).
  Run against the main checkout's prebuilt env (`<main-checkout>/.venv/bin/python -m pytest …`) and
  symlink `web/node_modules` from the main checkout.
- **The shared `.venv` imports `ccswitch.*` from the DEPLOY worktree, not your checkout.**
  `site-packages/__editable__.ccswitch-0.1.0.pth` points at
  `cc-account-switcher-deploy/src`, so edits under your own `src/ccswitch/` are silently ignored
  by tests — they pass or fail against *production* code. `server/*` is unaffected (pytest's
  rootdir wins). When touching `src/ccswitch/`, run with
  `PYTHONPATH=<your-checkout>/src` and confirm with
  `python -c "import ccswitch.ledger as m; print(m.__file__)"`. CI is unaffected: it installs from
  the checkout under test.
- API auth tests 401 unless `CCSWITCH_TAILNET_ALLOWLIST` includes the test identity (the real shell
  env sets a live allowlist). Pin it per-test, or run the full suite with
  `env -u CCSWITCH_TAILNET_ALLOWLIST CCSWITCH_DEV=1 pytest` (empty allowlist needs `CCSWITCH_DEV=1`).
- `create_all` never ALTERs existing tables, so `init_db` runs `_reconcile_columns` +
  `_assert_no_schema_drift` on **every** dialect (SQLite and Postgres) to ALTER-ADD missing columns.
  Add new model columns **nullable** and they are picked up automatically on both.
- A **NOT NULL** column still needs a real migration unless `_ddl_default_literal` can synthesize its
  default — reconcile logs and skips it, then the drift assert fails startup loudly.
- **Adding a MODEL (not just a column) means re-running the Postgres suite**, which is skipped unless
  `CCSWITCH_TEST_PG_URL` is set — so it is green locally and red in CI. Two hand-maintained lists in
  `server/tests/` enumerate every table and must gain an entry: `_REQUIRED_EXTRAS` in
  `test_postgres_compat.py` (NOT NULL columns the datetime sweep must supply) and, for a NOT NULL
  column with no synthesizable default, `RECONCILE_EXEMPT` in `test_schema_reconcile_coverage.py`.
- Nothing runs `alembic upgrade` at deploy time (and the prod DB has no `alembic_version` stamp — it was
  built by `create_all` at cutover). The revisions in `server/db/migrations/versions/` are the reviewable
  record of schema changes; reconcile is what actually applies them. Add a revision for any schema change
  anyway, and chain `down_revision` off the newest one.
- **`systemctl stop|restart ccswitch-daemon.service` touches every live session.** The daemon owns all
  running `claude` processes; a restart is never a "brief blip" for them. It drains in-flight turns on
  SIGTERM first (`server/ipc/drain_on_signal.py`, up to ~3 min / ~10 min mid-compaction), so the
  command blocks — expected, don't escalate. Prefer the deploy controller for code changes; for an env
  edit that needs a restart, do it when the Sessions page shows nothing mid-turn. Never restart a daemon
  whose installed unit still has `KillMode=control-group` while sessions are working — that kills them
  outright (`deploy/README.md` § "Stopping / restarting the daemon").

## Working norms

Concrete, operational discipline that backs constitution Principle VI (single source of truth / no
dead code) and IV/V (security-first, quality gates). Several map to installed skills — invoke the
skill, don't just recall the rule. `subagent-driven-development` ships with the `superpowers` plugin;
the others are user-local skills under `~/.claude/skills/` (if one is missing, follow the rule as
written here).

### Execute implementation plans subagent-driven — always

When a written plan reaches the execution-handoff step (brainstorming → writing-plans → execute),
**always** choose subagent-driven execution: a fresh subagent per task with review between tasks.
Never ask which mode to use and never default to inline batch execution. Skill:
`subagent-driven-development`.

### Before adding new code, find the existing source of truth

The most expensive bug shape is **N parallel implementations of one concept** (status maps, default
configs, enums, validation rules, design tokens, util helpers). **Before** adding a new constant,
helper, config list, or component, grep for what already exists and route through it. If it exists
but is wrong, fix it in place — adding a parallel "correct" copy *is* the anti-pattern.
- Python: search `server/` and `src/` for the symbol/string before writing a new helper or constant.
- Web: search `web/src/` (utils, lib, components, design tokens) before adding a new util or token.

Skill: `eliminating-parallel-implementations`.

### Purge replaced code in the same change — no half-dead code

When you replace a file, route, model, or function, delete the old version in the **same PR**. A
disconnected handler or orphaned module is a landmine: it gets imported by accident, drifts from the
new path, or is mistaken for canonical by the next grep. The only exception is a migration too large
for one PR — then mark the old path `# @deprecated — replaced by X, remove in #N` and track it in an
issue; otherwise, delete it.

### Audit recurring fix patterns — don't just patch

When you fix a bug whose *shape* could exist elsewhere (same anti-pattern, different file), capture
the pattern and sweep for siblings instead of fixing the one instance. The trigger is "this could
exist elsewhere," not "I'm sure it does" — false-positive audits are cheap; a missed second instance
of a silent bug is not. Skill: `capturing-fix-patterns`.

### Git safety

- Never `git push --force` — use `git push --force-with-lease`, which fails fast if the remote tip
  moved (e.g. a teammate or a sibling worktree pushed since you branched).
- Before rebasing a shared/feature branch, check for remote-only commits with
  `git log origin/<branch>...<branch>`. Pull or cherry-pick them first so a force-push doesn't
  silently drop merged work.

Skill: `safe-git-operations`.

### GitHub API — prefer GraphQL over REST for reads

`gh pr list` / `gh pr view` / `gh issue view` use REST under the hood and each costs a hit against
the shared 5,000-req/hr rate limit; a single `gh api graphql` query batches many reads into one
request. Use GraphQL for reads (`repo:steiner385/cc-account-switcher …`); reserve REST for mutations
that have no GraphQL path in `gh` (`gh pr create`, `gh pr merge`, `gh issue create/close`).
Skill: `github-via-graphql`.

### Issue auto-close keyword

GitHub closes a referenced issue on merge only when a closing keyword (`Fixes #N`, `Closes #N`,
`Resolves #N`) precedes the number in the **PR body or a commit message** — a bare `(#N)` links but
does NOT close. Put `Fixes #N` in the PR body for a full fix, `Refs #N` for a partial one.

## Copilot account type

ccswitch supports GitHub Copilot Pro+ accounts via the `whtsky/copilot2api` proxy binary, which
translates Anthropic API calls into Copilot API calls. Key operational notes:

**Provisioning the binary:** `CCSWITCH_ENABLE_COPILOT=true` must be set and the proxy binary must
be installed before adding Copilot accounts.

```bash
bash scripts/fetch-copilot-proxy.sh   # installs to ~/.local/lib/ccswitch/copilot2api
```

Or point to a custom binary: `CCSWITCH_COPILOT_PROXY_BIN=/path/to/copilot2api`.

**Copilot sessions behave differently from Anthropic sessions:**
- Suggestions and auto-summaries are disabled (`_pre_record` skips `suggester`/`summarizer`).
- `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=true` is injected — Claude Code disables MCP tool search for non-first-party
  base URLs, so this restores it for Copilot sessions.
- Usage is reported as premium-request quota (mapped to the `Usage` dataclass via
  `src/ccswitch/copilot.py:usage_from_proxy`), not session-reset tokens.
- The proxy runs as a supervised subprocess per account (see `CopilotProxyManager`), health-gated
  on `GET /usage`, with idle teardown after `CCSWITCH_COPILOT_IDLE_GRACE_S` (default 300 s).

**ToS caveat:** routing Claude sessions through the Copilot API may violate GitHub's ToS or
Anthropic's usage policies. This feature is provided for personal experimentation. Users are
responsible for ensuring their usage complies with applicable terms.

**Adding a Copilot account:** open the Add Account dialog → toggle to "GitHub Copilot" → enter a
name → click Add → follow the device-flow code at `github.com/login/device`.

## Server-side dictation (STT)

The mic button streams 16 kHz PCM to `/ws/stt` (`server/stt/`) where `faster-whisper`
(`base.en`, int8, CPU) transcribes it with Silero VAD endpointing; Web Speech is the fallback
when the edge does not advertise `sttEnabled` in `GET /api/config`.

- Enable with `CCSWITCH_ENABLE_STT=true` on the **edge** (needs the `stt` extra: the deploy
  controller installs `.[server,stt]`; CI/runners stay on `[server]`). First start downloads
  `Systran/faster-whisper-base.en` into the HuggingFace cache; the lifespan warms the model
  in a background thread.
- Knobs: `CCSWITCH_STT_MODEL` (`base.en`; `small.en` is ~1 s/tick on CPU — too slow),
  `CCSWITCH_STT_CPU_THREADS` (4), `CCSWITCH_STT_TICK_S` (1.0), `CCSWITCH_STT_MAX_CONCURRENT`
  (3), `CCSWITCH_STT_MAX_SESSION_S` (600).
- Policy lives in `server/stt/session.py` (pure, fake-engine tests); the real engine test is
  `server/tests/test_stt_whisper_integration.py`, gated on `CCSWITCH_TEST_STT=1`.
- Audio is never persisted or logged.

## Self-directed model switching

A running session can ask for a different model by ending a message with
`<!-- ccswitch:model=<tier> reason="..." -->`. The contract lives in
`server/sessions/model_request.py` (marker + instruction + parser, one module so the
system-prompt half and the scan half cannot drift).

- **Downgrades auto-apply** on the next turn; **upgrades park** for human approval in the
  existing `pending_model` columns. `resolve_self_directed_model_policy` composes this with
  the tier denylist and takes the stricter outcome — a **blocked tier stays blocked even as a
  downgrade**.
- A parked hold can be approved **at a different model** (`POST /sessions/{id}/model-approval`
  with `{"decision": "approve", "model": "opus"}`). Only `block` refuses a counter-offer.
- **Never route an approval through `set_model_for_session()`** — it re-runs the policy and
  re-parks, so every approval would re-ask for approval. Approvals use the low-level
  `driver.set_model()` / `_spawn_session(model=…)` paths.
- Guards (`server/sessions/self_model_guards.py`): same-tier dedupe, a cap of
  `CCSWITCH_SELF_MODEL_SWITCH_CAP` (default 3) auto-applies per session, a flip-flop halt, and
  a drop once a human has amended a request for that tier.
- Kill switch: `CCSWITCH_SELF_MODEL_SWITCH_ENABLED=false` stops both the prompt instruction
  and any acting on a marker.
- Audit `model_approval.approve` carries `{requested, applied}` — requested ≠ applied is the
  metric for whether sessions self-assess accurately.

## Codex adaptations

- Treat references to “Claude” as references to the active coding agent unless they
  specifically describe the Claude binary, Anthropic API, Claude sessions, or
  `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`.
- Do not add a Claude `Co-Authored-By` trailer to Codex-authored commits. Use the
  configured Git identity and add an AI attribution trailer only when the user
  supplies one. This overrides only the attribution rule in the shared guidance.
- Repo-scoped reusable workflows live under `.agents/skills/`; invoke the matching
  skill when the shared guidance names one.
- Codex lifecycle policy is wired by `.codex/config.toml`; command restrictions live
  in `.codex/rules/`. Keep both aligned with the governance source of truth in
  `server/sdlc/governance.py`.

## Code review

Before reviewing a pull request or branch, read `.claude/REVIEW.md` in full and apply
it as the provider-neutral review policy. Report only allowed categories, use its
severity tags, respect the nit cap and exclusions, and preserve separation of duties.
